The enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of natural progesterone, and its activity can be influenced by various drugs, leading to changes in progesterone levels or effects. 2. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered to avoid this interaction. 3. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. 4. Natural progesterone increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Natural progesterone increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. The combination of natural progesterone with bazedoxifene or conjugated estrogens may result in pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing breast tenderness. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Natural progesterone increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Betrixaban dosage should be reduced to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 8. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used to avoid this interaction. 9.
